extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to ARR/EMNLP 2025 (ACL community); program chairs, reviewers, and area chairs
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and operational requirements for author reviewer volunteering, reviewer qualifications, incentives, exemptions, and sanctions for the ARR May 2025 (EMNLP 2025) review cycle. Covers who must register, who may be assigned reviews, what counts as a qualified reviewer/AC, logistics and deadlines, and positive/negative incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author registration and confirmation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must complete a form to confirm their OpenReview profile is complete and they will serve if asked. (This form becomes available in the author console after submission.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission the OpenReview console will show a link to author registration (e.g. Authors group). All authors must register before 48 hours after submission deadline (i.e. May 21 EoD AoE for EMNLP 2025). The submitting authors should ensure all authors on the team are aware of this requirement and sign up to review on time. Authors selected as reviewers will receive kick-off emails with instructions and links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any qualified author may be assigned to review
rubrics_metrics.description: Any qualified author on a submission may be assigned to review for the cycle; based on qualifications, not all authors may actually be assigned reviews, but they all need to sign up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach increases the reviewer pool and is expected to lower average review load per reviewer (~4). Authors should coordinate within teams to check that all (meta-)reviews assigned to the team are submitted on time and in accordance with guidelines. Nominating non-author reviewers will no longer be possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'qualified' reviewer (author)
rubrics_metrics.description: An author is 'qualified' if they have (a) at least two papers in main ACL events or Findings, plus (b) at least one more paper in the ACL Anthology or a major ML/AI venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues considered 'main ACL' are: ACL, CL, CoLing, CoNLL, EACL, EMNLP, HLT, IJCNLP / AACL, LREC, NAACL, TACL, *SEM, COLM. Major ML/AI venues considered: AAAI, CVPR, ECCV, FAccT, ICCV, ICLR, ICML, IJCAI, JAIR, JMLR, NIPS, NeurIPS, TMLR, TPAMI. When there are no qualified reviewers for a paper, ARR will consider reviewer candidates case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer duty exemptions (case-by-case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review duty exemptions are possible on a case-by-case basis (e.g., parental leave). Anyone serving in another capacity (e.g., as an Area Chair) does not need to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption requests and compliance checks may take longer due to a larger reviewer pool; desk-rejects due to non-compliance are possible and could happen later in the cycle. If an author is serving in another capacity, that will be indicated in the registration form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for being 'highly irresponsible'
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers or chairs deemed 'highly irresponsible' by program chairs will not be able to commit their work to ARR, or (re-)submit their work to the subsequent ARR cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of 'highly irresponsible' behavior include non-submission of (meta-)reviews on time without due warning, extremely terse reviews for good-faith submissions, egregious violations of guidelines on LLM use and professional tone. Consequences include teams of papers with such reviewers/chairs as authors having to sit out a cycle. EMNLP 2025 PCs published an initial set of criteria (link provided) and these criteria will be iteratively developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive incentives for great reviewers and chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Great reviewers and chairs will receive increased recognition during conferences and may win a free virtual attendee voucher for an ACL event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ACL peer review committee developed an incentives policy; see the full policy for details. Recognition and occasional vouchers are intended to reward exemplary reviewing and chairing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recruitment strategy: mandatory qualified-author reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: ARR will implement the CVPR-style approach where all qualified authors on any submission are required to review for the cycle (implemented starting May 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to be simpler than proportional-request calculations used earlier. Primary reviewers may mentor subreviewers instead of performing all reviews personally. Nominating non-author reviewers will no longer be possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring/subreviewer option
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary reviewers are allowed to mentor subreviewers instead of performing reviews themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This option aims to allow senior authors to distribute reviewing work and mentor junior members; the system still expects the team to ensure assigned (meta-)reviews are submitted on time and follow guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics and deadlines for May 2025 cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration, review, and meta-review deadlines and process logistics for the cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration deadline: within 48 hours after submission deadline (May 21 EoD AoE for EMNLP 2025). Planned review deadline: June 18. Meta-review deadline: July 15. Authors selected as reviewers will receive kick-off emails with instructions and links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for requiring prior ACL Anthology presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring prior work in ACL Anthology helps ensure reviewers share the community's norms and expectations and prevents submissions being judged by different-community standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interdisciplinary submissions usually have some connection to the target community; ARR will consider exceptions when there are no qualified reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chair (AC) qualification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs must meet three criteria: either a completed PhD or a main conference *CL publication from more than 5 years ago; four papers in main ACL events or Findings; two additional papers in either main ACL events or major ML/AI venues; and extensive reviewing experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists of main ACL and major ML/AI venues are provided and both main track and Findings papers count. This is a modification of prior AC requirements to align with the reviewer qualification policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: No nomination of non-author reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominating non-author reviewers will no longer be possible in the May 2025 cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously non-authors could be nominated (e.g., a senior postdoc); under the new approach that option is removed, though primary reviewers can mentor subreviewers.
